questions.question: The first semester scores of six students indicated that Raman immediate scored higher than Ritesh, but he is second lower to Harshita. If Ankur is the second-lowest scorer, then what could be the position of Raghav?
questions.solution:
Given:

**1) Raman immediate scored higher than Ritesh, but he is second lower to Harshita.**

Harshita > ______ > Raman > Ritesh

**2) Ankur is the second-lowest scorer.**

Harshita > ______ > Raman > Ritesh > Ankur > _______

**Now, Raghav position may be second and may be last.**

Now we check all the given options:

Option (1) Between Raman and Ritesh → False (Nobody scores between Raman and Ritesh)

Option (2) Just below Ritesh → False (Ankur is just below the Ritesh)

Option (3) Just above Harshita → False (Harshit is score highest)

Option (4) Just above Raman → True (Raghav position maybe just above Raman)

Hence, “Option (4)” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following number series?

256, 123, 66, ?, 18, 6
questions.solution:
**The pattern follows here is:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8f9ff339d844ea4cf5c3594920fd33ebc9a204dbd94397cf312e2f0c22e529f.png] 

(256 – 10) ÷ 2 = 246 ÷ 2 = 123

(123 + 9) ÷ 2 = 132 ÷ 2 = 66

**(66 - 8) ÷ 2 = 58 ÷ 2 = 29**

(29 + 7) ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18

(18 - 6) ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6

Hence, correct answer is **“29”**

questions.solution:
Total person:- A, B, C, D, E and F sitting along the sides of a heptagon table facing the centre

1) D is second to the right of A

2) B is second to the right of F, who is to the immediate right of A.

**Note:-** **G and E position is not fixed so we decide the position of E according to the options.**

Now, check the options for the sitting position of E

Option (1) Immediate left of F **→ **False

Option (2) Immediate left of B **→ **False

**Thus, E is** Immediate right of C is not given in any option so Immediate right of C will be the correct.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. 

**Statements:**

All Machines are Tools.

No Tool is a Computer.

**Conclusions:**

I. No Machine is a Computer.

II. Some Computers are Tools.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
Statements:

All Machines are Tools.

No Tool is a Computer.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d6e3f484c0b43d83038ac46e0e21cdb47ddd95779d6b228d8c12df298a33bde.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No Machine is a Computer → Ture (because all machines are tools and no tool is a computer so definitely no machine is a computer)

II. Some Computers are Tools → False (because statement given no Tool is a Computer so some computers are tools it is not possible)

Hence, “**Only conclusion I follow**” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which of the given options is the most suitable to fill in the blank?

**16 : 128 : : 4 : ________**
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

Let (1st number : 2nd number)

(1st number) × (1st number **÷ 2**) = 2nd number

Now follow the steps:

16 : 128

=> 16 × (16 ÷ 2) = 16 × 8 = 128 = 2nd number

Similarly,

4 : ?

**=> 4 × (4 ÷ 2) = 4 × 2 = 8 = 2nd number**

Hence, "8" is correct answer.
